observation_summary: The CMAESOptimizer was performing poorly near the upper bound because it was mapping the parameter range to [0, 1] using an incorrect transformation formula that caused precision issues.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved rewriting the transformation logic (the encoding and decoding methods) used to map parameters into the [0, 1] interval. The original implementation used an incorrect formula that introduced precision bias. This is a fundamental change to the computational procedure (the algorithm) used to handle bounds, rather than a simple value assignment or a missing guard.
evidence_used: The bug report states the optimizer maps the fitted parameter range into [0, 1] and that the unit of least precision (ulp) causes resolution issues.
The fix_diff_oracle shows a change in the mathematical formula for 'res[i]' in both the encoding and decoding methods.
The fix_diff_oracle also updates the boundary check logic to use the newly encoded boundaries, which is part of the corrected algorithmic approach for handling bounds.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix includes updated boundary checks, these checks are a consequence of the corrected encoding algorithm. The root cause is the incorrect mathematical transformation of the parameters.
The fix is not about setting a wrong constant or variable, but about changing the entire computational formula used for mapping values.
